claims.statement: NACP defaults to INFO text logging on stdout with JSON logging and all three OTLP signals disabled; HCL loading starts from defaults and only stdout/stderr are accepted as local output destinations.

Text, JSON, and OTLP log handlers are independent fanout destinations, so enabling JSON does not disable default text output; the demo intentionally enables text stdout and JSON stderr alongside OTLP.

A shared Leveler maps DEBUG, INFO, WARN, and ERROR to both slog and minimum OTLP severity and updates both variables on Set; unknown levels panic, and logger names are passed to the OTLP bridge as scopes rather than automatically attached to local records.
The bootstrap logger is INFO-and-above stdout text unless -bootstrap-json-logger selects JSON; run replaces it with configured logging, and log_level has moved to telemetry.logging.level.

SetupOTelSDK independently enables OTLP HTTP log, metric, and trace exporters without NACP-specific exporter options, delegating configuration to standard exporter environment handling; the collector helper configures OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_INSECURE, and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf.

Production telemetry uses an explicit resource with service.name=nacp and service.version from the executable version variable, defaulting to dev; SetupOTelSDK uses NewWithAttributes rather than environment resource detection.
example/otel demonstrates injecting OTEL semantic conventions into admitted workloads through inject_otel, not enabling NACP's own telemetry exports.

Admission enforcement follows controller return values and route handling rather than log severity: register and plan abort on admission errors, whereas validate-only carries validator errors in request context for response augmentation.

JobHandler creates admission.apply, mutators.process, mutate: <name>, validators.process, and validate: <name> spans using tracer scope github.com/mxab/nacp; admission.apply and invocation spans carry nomad.job.id, invocation spans carry the relevant controller-name attribute, and successful reported mutations add mutated=true.

The validate-only route calls mutation and validation phase methods directly and therefore has no admission.apply span; missing job IDs are represented as empty strings on the spans that attach that attribute.
Mutator errors stop the chain and prevent validation on the combined admission path; validators otherwise receive isolated copies of the final mutated job and aggregate their failures.

Non-nil controller invocation errors set invocation-span error status and record the error; a nil mutator job sets error status and increments errors without RecordError, while phase and admission.apply spans do not explicitly mirror child error status.
NACP wraps incoming proxy requests with otelhttp using operation name /, and buildServer supplies a remoteutil-instrumented Nomad transport for both upstream proxying and token resolution.

Webhook mutator and validator calls preserve the admission context using NewRequestWithContext and a shared instrumented transport with a 30-second client timeout; InstrumentedTransport installs otelhttptrace after the transport span starts so connection spans are children of it.
ApplyProviders installs a TraceContext and Baggage composite propagator; NACP-Client-IP, NACP-Accessor-ID, and X-Forwarded-For are separate admission-context headers rather than trace-parent headers.
Controller and proxy context-aware logs pass the active request/span context to logging, but post-admission job logs use plain Debug, so not every record has request trace correlation.
The five generated NACP controller instruments are Float64Counters in meter scope nacp.controller with only validator.name or mutator.name as explicit data-point attributes, not job ID.

nacp.validator.warning.count adds the number of warnings returned by each validator even alongside an error, while nacp.validator.error.count adds one per non-nil invocation error rather than one per constituent error message; job-copy failure happens before this instrumented invocation path.

nacp.mutator.error.count adds one for an invocation error or nil returned job before aborting the chain; nacp.mutator.warning.count adds returned warning count only after success with a non-nil job, and nacp.mutator.mutation.count adds one when mutated is true.

Built-in JSON-patch mutators derive their mutation boolean from successful PatchJob application with len(patch)>0, not a semantic before/after diff or changed-field count; controller mutation increments are not rolled back when later admission fails.

Controller error counters are not rejected-job totals: multiple validators can fail one request, validate-only uses the same counters, and failures before controller invocation can bypass them; HTTP instrumentation provides a separate metric population.

Severity is log-site-specific: local OPA validator policy warnings and errors are logged at DEBUG, webhook validation errors at ERROR, and proxy admission failure at WARN, independent of their returned enforcement errors.

DEBUG telemetry can disclose sensitive serialized post-admission job/request content and OPA decision results; sanitizing the resolved ACL token to omit SecretID and ExpirationTTL does not redact arbitrary job or policy data.

The otelslog bridge now stores error-valued attributes on the record's error field for OTLP exception.message/exception.type export, requiring old error-attribute queries to change; migration of test log body/attribute types to shared attribute APIs is separately a test API change rather than itself a runtime format change.

Runtime initializes configured logging, then enabled telemetry providers, then OPA and server/controller instrumentation; SDK setup constructs enabled trace, metric, and log providers in that order before installing globals, with trace/log batching and a periodic metric reader.

An exporter constructor failure causes SetupOTelSDK to shut down previously registered providers and run to abort startup; cleanup joins errors and clears its callback list, while ApplyProviders only replaces non-nil providers and therefore does not reset disabled signals' preexisting globals.

On interrupt or SIGTERM, run attempts HTTP server shutdown with a 30-second deadline, then deferred telemetry shutdown uses context.Background and joins errors into the return error; production SetupOTelSDK exposes shutdown rather than a separate flush callback.

SetupOTelSDKWith flushes only tracer and meter providers, registers tracer-provider, meter-provider, and trace-exporter shutdown, and leaves lifecycle of its caller-supplied logger provider to the caller; tests collect/read telemetry before teardown.

pkg/o11y/metric.go is generated from registry definitions in pkg/o11y/nacp.yaml and common.yaml with templates/registry/go metric template and Weaver settings; root generate.go still targets ./o11y for registry/output rather than the inspected pkg/o11y layout, so its regeneration command is not a verified recipe for this layout.

Telemetry tests use a log recorder, manual metric reader, and in-memory span exporter to check all five controller counters, HTTP metrics, and logs, but the integration span assertion only checks a minimum count rather than exact parentage; separate tests cover fanout/level changes and actual OTLP logs via a container collector.
Telemetry test setup installs process-global providers and the collector helper mutates process environment, so concurrent global-mutating tests require isolation.
